questions.prompt: A team gives an assistant 30 tools. Which statement matches the vendors' docs?

options.text: The tool definitions are free, because they are only setup data.
options.explanation: Both vendors say the opposite. Anthropic counts the tools parameter in input tokens, and OpenAI says function definitions are billed as input tokens.

options.text: The tool definitions are billed as input tokens on requests that include them.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's pricing page counts the tools parameter as input tokens. OpenAI's function calling guide says definitions are billed as input tokens.

options.text: Only the tool results are billed, not the definitions.
options.explanation: Results are billed too, but so are the definitions.

questions.prompt: On most Claude models, what does Anthropic's pricing page say a prompt cache read costs?

options.explanation: Right. A few models use a lower multiplier, but 0.1x is the standard one on the page.
That is the price of a 5-minute cache write, not a read.

options.text: The same as base input; caching only saves time.
options.explanation: Caching reduces cost as well as delay. A cache read is priced below base input.

questions.prompt: Both vendors document a Batch API. What is the trade-off?

options.text: About half price, but results are not instant.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic lists a 50% discount and OpenAI lists a 50% discount. The work runs asynchronously.

options.text: Full price, but a higher quality model answers.
options.explanation: Batch gives a discount. It does not change the model.

options.text: About half price, and answers still arrive in a second.
options.explanation: Batch is asynchronous. Anthropic says most batches finish in under an hour, and OpenAI says within 24 hours.
